To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aroma of lager beer is composed of 1,3-butadiene and 1,3-pentadiene and that 3-methyl-1,3-butene is the most important odorant in lager beer.

the aroma profile of lager beer is dominated by a complex mixture of aldehydes, esters, and higher alcohols that are formed during fermentation, and that the sensory properties of beer can be predicted by a mathematical model that is based on the concentration of these aroma compounds in beer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensory evaluation and chemical identification of lager beer aromas.

the development and application of a novel method for the determination of the volatile composition of beer, which is based on the combination of solid-phase microextraction (SPME) with gas chromatography (GC) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS).
the development of a method to determine the aroma composition and intensity of a product, in this case, lager beer, and the use of that information to determine the sensory quality of the product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aroma profile of lager beer is a complex mixture of hundreds of volatile aroma compounds, and that the aroma of lager beer can be described as a mixture of fruity esters, hop-derived compounds, aldehydes, alcohols, and miscellaneous compounds.
the sensory evaluation of the beer aroma is a more reliable and sensitive method to determine the aroma quality and the sensory properties of the beer than the chemical analysis.
sensory analysis is a more reliable and valid method for the determination of beer aroma quality than GC and GC/MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to show the feasibility of a new analytical technique for beer aroma analysis.
we were able to show that sensory and chemical analysis of beer aroma can be performed in a similar fashion.

sensory evaluation of lager beers is a reliable method for detecting differences among beers, and that gas chromatography and GC/MS are useful tools for identifying the compounds responsible for these differences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to improve the sensitivity and specificity of our current methods for detecting the presence of adulterants in food.

the sensory properties of beer can be described in terms of a small set of aroma-active compounds, which are present at low concentration in the beer and which are not necessarily the most abundant compounds in the headspace of the beer.
the sensory properties of a beer are not only influenced by the aroma-active compounds but also by the aroma-inactive compounds.
